date_note: Some coverage dates the announcement to 16 November; SecurityWeek published on 17 November.
exec: Investors are backing purpose-built defensive AI models as AI-driven attacks grow; expect more agent-based security offerings.
geo_basis: company HQ (Tel Aviv and San Francisco)
plain: A young security company that builds its own AI models to help defenders spot attacks raised $125 million and is now valued at $1 billion.
summary: Cybersecurity startup Corma raised $125 million in a Series A led by NEA, with Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures and Coatue also investing. The round takes total funding to $185 million and the valuation to $1 billion. Founded in 2025 and based in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, Corma trains frontier foundation models for defence and runs them as AI agents alongside existing security tools.
title: Corma raises $125 million Series A at $1 billion valuation for defensive AI models
